region: Riverhead · North Fork of Long Island, New York
about: RGNY is the New York estate of the Rivero González family, Mexican winegrowers who planted their first vines in Parras, Coahuila, in 1998. In 2018 they bought Martha Clara Vineyards on Sound Avenue in Riverhead, a 205-acre property on Long Island’s North Fork, and relaunched it as RGNY in 2019. Winemaker Lilia Pérez, raised in Mexico City and trained in Bordeaux, moved to the estate in 2018 after working with the family’s Mexican winery, and works with some 87 acres of vines and fifteen grape varieties.

The North Fork is a narrow finger of farmland between Long Island Sound and Peconic Bay, where the surrounding water gives a long, moderate growing season and keeps acidity fresh, well suited to sparkling wine. This one is made in the traditional Champagne method from hand-harvested Chardonnay and Pinot Noir grown on sandy loam, and rests on its lees for 24 months. It is finished with zero dosage, meaning no sugar is added after disgorgement, so it is as dry as sparkling wine comes.

Zero dosage leaves nothing to mask the fruit, so the style rewards careful grape growing and patient aging on the lees. The winery describes bright green apple and light buttery notes with crisp acidity and medium weight, and Wine Enthusiast scored it 92 points. It is made in small quantities, about 2,640 bottles in the release listed by the New York merchant Zachys, from vineyards farmed under sustainable certification.
